A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RegCache by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and retrieval experiments, token analyses, component ablations, and weight-only quantization results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains and updates original experiments and adds low-bit evaluations, comparator results, controlled analyses, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 materially revise register construction. V1 selects an individual register from 20 candidates through a joint search over candidate identity and repetition count. V3 increases the candidate count to 100, averages their key-value caches, and searches over repetitions of the averaged cache.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k classification, MS-COCO retrieval, and transfer evaluation on Stanford Cars, Flowers-102, Food-101, and CIFAR-100. The ImageNet-9 foreground/background study and Wikitext-2 LLM diagnostic are also retained. Added quantization configurations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated comparisons with FIMA-Q in Tables 8–9, adapted QuaRot in Table 13, and Jiang et al.'s test-time register approach in Table 14. These comparisons are absent from v1, although FIMA-Q and Jiang et al. were already cited. Existing quantization comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds W4A4 evaluations and W6A6 retrieval results, changes AWQ activation precision from A32 to A16, and reduces the token-norm analysis from 1,000 to 500 images. Table 2 excludes naïve quantization from summary gains and changes Best Δ from the difference between best accuracies to the largest baseline-specific gain. New controls and latency measurements introduce additional evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: V3 adds an outlier-range control in Appendix A, prefix-insertion-layer sensitivity in Figure 8, and wall-clock efficiency analysis. Table 6 expands component ablations to SigLIP2. Conversely, the norm analysis removes DINOv2 and normal-token measurements, while Figures 2 and 5 remove hidden-state curves. The foreground/background and tokenization studies are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same mean and ± values from 64 images, and Figure 3 retains its shaded bands. Neither version reports benchmark seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many results change alongside the revised method: Table 2's W8A8 naïve-plus-RegCache accuracy changes from 61.44 to 59.71 for CLIP and from 68.65 to 72.35 for SigLIP2. V3 also adds extensive low-bit, comparator, diagnostic, and latency results. AWQ scores are replaced under A16 rather than A32, so their changes cannot be treated as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix B adds a stylized spiked-vector lemma and proof: cosine similarity approaches 1 for spikes in the same coordinate and 0 for different coordinates. V1 contains no corresponding proof. This provides a focused mathematical explanation of the existing token-similarity observation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a training-free method that combines middle-layer register prefixing and token deletion to suppress outliers and improve quantized vision encoders. V3 emphasizes activation quantization and plug-in compatibility, but these contributions and their intended scope were already present in v1.

C2.justification: V3 adds channel alignment as an explanation for token similarity and attributes measured latency overhead to prefix-related memory traffic. Limitations shift toward model- and quantizer-specific choices of prefix and deletion counts. Its expanded ablation discussion emphasizes synergy, although the statement that either component alone performs worse than the baseline is not consistently supported by Table 6.

D1.justification: V3 newly reports RTX 4090, RTX A6000, and A6000 Ada hardware, plus approximately one hour of RTN-based search on an RTX 4090. It documents whole-validation-set latency measurement and Hadamard-rotation exceptions for value and output projections. These disclosures are absent from v1.

R1.justification: V3 adds QuaRot, SpinQuant, and ViDiT-Q references, expands discussion of the previously cited FIMA-Q, and directly positions RegCache against test-time registers in Appendix M. Its broader relationship to LLM prefixing and vision-transformer registers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from Post-training Quantization to Activation Quantization, Sections 3.2 and 3.3 exchange order, and prose and cross-references receive localized revisions. The main narrative structure remains recognizable. Appendices are reorganized, and the LLM-use disclosure is removed.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn; Figures 2 and 5 use logarithmic norm axes and fewer traces; tables are expanded and reorganized; and Figure 8 and several comparison tables are added. V3 also resolves the overlap between Table 6 and body text visible in v1.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens assessment through low-bit evaluations, direct test-time-register comparisons, targeted controls, measured latency, and hardware/search-cost disclosures. However, new inconsistencies limit confidence: Table 8 assigns CLIP/OpenCLIP full-precision values inconsistently with Table 2, and Appendix D claims FIMA-Q improvements across all models despite its reported SigLIP2 decreases. The additional usable evidence supports a net improvement, tempered by these reporting problems.
